title: Why songs get stuck in your head

lines.text: It's two in the morning, and your brain is playing the same ten seconds of a song. Again.
You don't even like this song.
Scientists call it an earworm, and most people get one at least once a week.
Ever noticed it's always just a tiny piece of the song?
Psychologists call it the Zeigarnik effect. You remember interrupted things better than finished ones.
So when you only catch part of a chorus, your brain keeps it open, like a browser tab you can't close.
Catchy songs make it worse. Simple melody, lots of repetition, and one surprising jump.
The good news? Science found a few fixes.
One. Chew gum. A study at the University of Reading found it cut down earworms, because it keeps the muscles you'd sing with busy.
Two. Listen to the whole song, so your brain gets its ending.
Three. Give your brain a puzzle. Not too easy, not too hard.
And don't try to block it. Fighting a thought makes it come back stronger.
Anyway. Good luck getting this one out of your head.
